catalog_quote: In Avar, stress typically targets the first or the second syllable, but the conditioning for stress placement often evades explanation. Stress variants for some lexical items are possible (Charachidzé 1981:18), and there is considerable dialectal variation ... Most nouns carry stress on the second syllable, though exceptions and minimal pairs are numerous: k’úlal ‘key.PL’, k’ulál ‘lock’; ráʁi ‘fight’, raʁí ‘balcony’ (Isakov 1981: 88). There are productive morphological processes that derive minimal pairs based on stress ... Many case affixes don’t shift stress ... On the other hand, some do, so that certain case forms differ in stress only ... Many masdars and numerals are stressed on the initial syllable, and most verbs are stressed on the last syllable of the root/stem. Some verbal affixes, such as iterative and evidential ones, can attract stress out of the stress window ... Mikailov…

sources.quote: 'Kak izvestno, v avarskom literaturnom jazyke udarenie ne perexodit dal'še vtorogo ot načala sloga' [in literary Avar stress does not go beyond the second syllable from the beginning]; Russian loans should be nativised accordingly (agítacija, advákat, ínvalid, apérator...). Also line 108: disyllables 'where stress falls on the first syllable' (naku, nisu...) as one lexical class.
sources.locator: the text (right column, section on orthography rule 3, stress in loans)

sources.citation: Xasbulatova, X. M. 2016. Osobennosti sovremennyx orfoèpičeskix norm v russkom i avarskom jazykax. Izvestija Dagestanskogo gos. ped. universiteta. Obščestvennye i gumanitarnye nauki 10(4): 140-144. (open, CyberLeninka; pedagogical/contrastive article)
sources.quote: 'Udarenie v avarskom jazyke možet prixodit'sja na ljuboj slog, no v bol'šinstve slučaev padaet na pervyj ili vtoroj slog i ne zavisit ot količestva slogov v slove. Začastuju različie meždu dvumja slovami vyraženo mestom udarenija, naprimer, ʕintʼí (šipovnik) – ʕíntʼi (razvorot byka na paxote). Pri izmenenii slova udarenie menjaetsja s odnogo sloga na drugoj: saʕát – sáʕal.' Stress dynamic but weaker than Russian; not fixed; lexical minimal pairs; shifts under inflection.

sources.quote: 'V avarskom jazyke ono fiksirovano na pervom sloge ili na vtorom [sloge] slova [7]' — stress on the first or second syllable of the word; no conditioning given. Passing remark only.

sources.citation: Dybo, Vladimir A., Sergej L. Nikolaev & Sergej A. Starostin. 1978. A tonological hypothesis on the origin of paradigmatic accent systems. Estonian Papers in Phonetics 1978, 16-20. (image PDF from inslav.ru; scanned with tesseract, 300 dpi)
sources.quote: 'Avar possesses a system of three accent paradigms - two with immobile stress on the root (stress on the first syllable - paradigm A, stress on the second - paradigm B) and one with mobile stress (paradigm C).' Paradigm examples B: 'flea' gen. -ól, C: cer 'fox' gen. car-ál, pl. cur-dul; paradigm A linked historically to pharyngealization+labialization, i.e. lexically specified.
sources.locator: p. 18, section '2. Avaro-Andian languages' (scanned the text)

sources.note: The only full phonological analysis of Avar stress in a Western language (accentual paradigms, lexical 'tone' pattern, articulatory accent, closed-second-syllable weight clause); StressTyp2's weight-driven coding that contradicts our lexical reading derives from it, and we hold it only as an StressTyp2 quotation carried over second-hand from StressTyp2. Reading it first-hand would settle the weight/heavy sub-fields and the StressTyp2 'partly' note.
